methodology: Quality analysis of OSM data unsing the ohsome dashboard.
name: syria-osm-data-quality
notes:
This dataset provides insights into the data quality of [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/) (OSM) data in Syria. It has been created using the OSM data quality analysis of [ohsome](https://dashboard.ohsome.org/).

 Different indicators are used to asses the data quality depending on the selected topic, for further information regarding the calculation of the quality indicators see the [Github](https://github.com/GIScience/ohsome-quality-api) repository. The OSM data quality analysis is available for different topics either as a CSV or as a Geopackage file. The quality analysis is available in three units: admin level 0, admin level 1 and hexagons. Each zip file contains all three units for the selected topic. The unit of analysis is defined by [geoboundaries](https://www.geoboundaries.org/) country borders.

Attributes of the CSV/ Geopackage file:

- **[unit]_id**: Unit of quality analysis.

- **ADM0_name**: Name of the country.

- **ADM0_iso**: ISO3 country code.

- **result_value_[indicator]**: Calculated result of OSM data quality for the respective indicator. Ranges between 0 and 1.

 Different indicators are available for each topic. Check out the [Topic Catalog](https://dashboard.ohsome.org/en/) to see which indicators are relevant for which topic.

This dataset is one of many [HeiGIT exports on HDX](https://data.humdata.org/organization/heidelberg-institute-for-geoinformation-technology). See the [HeiGIT](https://heigit.org/) website for more information.

We are looking forward to hearing about your use-case! Feel free to reach out to us and tell us about your research at [communications@heigit.org](mailto:communications@heigit.org) – we would be happy to amplify your work.

organization.title: HeiGIT (Heidelberg Institute for Geoinformation Technology)
organization.description:
HeiGIT (Heidelberg Institute for Geoinformation Technology) performs applied research relating to geographic information. Results and data are made freely available for the benefit of the environment and society through stakeholders such as researchers and aid organizations & associations.

The core foci of HeiGIT range from supporting humanitarian missions with customized geodata, to developing intelligent routing solutions for disasters or heatwaves. HeiGIT also implements innovative methods from the fields of spatial data processing and machine learning to analyze, enrich, and visualize geodata (e.g. OpenStreetMap data), as well as offering practical data analysis for climate protection initiatives.

HeiGIT gGmbH was founded in 2019 as an affiliated institute of Heidelberg University, with core funding from the Klaus Tschira Foundation.
